## Context / Problem

The project needs a repository-wide audit of documentation and source comments against the operator standards recorded below. Future developers and agents need an evidence-based remediation proposal before any project file changes are authorized.

## Audit standards

The standards baseline is the operator instruction dated 2026-08-20, preserved in this ticket through the following requirements.

- Prose must not use an em dash, en dash, spaced hyphen, semicolon, or a colon that connects or introduces a clause within a sentence.
- A colon may introduce a list of items or act as a structural label. Spoken narration must contain no colon.
- Hyphens are limited to compound words, technical names, identifiers, Markdown list bullets, table separators, horizontal rules, code operators, or SQL operators. A plain hyphen must not replace a dash.
- Every Markdown paragraph remains one logical line. Line breaks remain only where Markdown structure requires them.
- Writing uses a formal voice with precise verbs, complete sentences, no contractions, no colloquialisms, and no casual connectors.
- Filler or authenticity padding must be deleted. The prohibited filler list contains `real`, `actual`, `genuine`, `live` when used as a value adjective, `simply`, `just`, `quietly`, `seamlessly`, `robust`, `powerful`, `leverage`, `truly`, `in real time`, `concretely`, and `today` when used for emphasis rather than as a date.
- Authenticity padding phrases such as `not a placeholder`, `live for this run`, `the thing that matters`, or `this is not a mock` must not appear. Writing describes the mechanism or source instead of claiming authenticity.
- A noun remains unmodified unless an adjective selects one option from several.
- Tickets preserve the history of work for future developers or agents.
- ADRs preserve key decisions that introduce architectural invariants needing more visibility than tickets. Future developers or agents are their primary audience.
- Internal project documentation explains the current development processes, architecture, or codebase. It references tickets or ADRs when historical context is necessary instead of repeating material that has no future use.
- External documentation teaches clients who do not develop rebar or understand its internals. It uses concise language focused on using rebar.
- Shipped help follows the external documentation model. It supports discovery and directs users to relevant information shipped with rebar.
- Comments provide developer context required to understand code. Comments are not conversations, historical records, or restatements of the code. References to tickets or ADRs are encouraged when they supply necessary context.

## Approach

Survey every maintained documentation surface and source comment category. Classify each finding by intended audience and durable record type. Compare factual claims with code, configuration, generated help sources, tests, ADRs, and ticket history. Record findings in a session log. Ask independent agents to inspect non-overlapping shards. Ask a later reviewer group to challenge the consolidated proposals. The fan-out by repository surface follows `docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md`. Separate shards reduce omissions within large document families. The later challenge pass evaluates the complete set, which exposes cross-shard duplication, misplacement, unsupported claims, and coverage gaps. Present the filtered proposal list for operator approval.

## Scope

- Root contributor and client documents, package metadata, repository policies, templates, and workflow text.
- Internal documents under `docs/`, including ADRs and indexes.
- External documents, packaged guides, command help, MCP descriptions, examples, and other shipped user guidance.
- Developer comments and docstrings in maintained source, scripts, tests, and configuration files.
- Relevant ticket history needed to distinguish historical records from current-state documentation.
- Read-only repository inspection. No project file edits, gates, commits, or pushes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The inventory names every maintained surface in scope plus every explicit exclusion. Verification uses a session log coverage table.
- [ ] Every proposal cites a repository path, symbol, command output, ADR, or ticket as evidence. Verification uses the proposal evidence field.
- [ ] Every proposal names one target documentation type plus its audience. Verification uses the proposal classification fields.
- [ ] Every proposal states one remediation action plus one destination. Verification uses the proposal action fields.
- [ ] Every factual correction identifies the implementation, configuration, test, or effective help source used to establish expected behavior. Verification uses the proposal citations.
- [ ] Exploration agents inspect non-overlapping shards. Verification uses one session log report for each shard.
- [ ] Filtering agents challenge every consolidated proposal for evidence quality, factual accuracy, completeness, placement, duplication, and prose conformance. Verification assigns every draft item a retained, revised, merged, or rejected status.
- [ ] The final proposal text conforms to the audit standards in this ticket. Verification uses a punctuation scan plus manual diction review.
- [ ] No project file changes exist at handoff. Verification uses final worktree status plus diff checks.
- [ ] The filtered proposal appears in a ticket comment. Verification uses `rebar show minimum-rainy-fawn`.
- [ ] The filtered proposal appears in the operator response. Verification uses the completed response.
